# gitmoap_channel_members (Data Source)

List a private channel's members. Who reads a private channel or a direct conversation, in the order they were added. Who reads any other channel follows from access to its group, so it has no member list.

The token needs `channel:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "channel_id" {
  type = string
}

data "gitmoap_channel_members" "example" {
  channel_id = var.channel_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) The channel

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) Members, in the order they were added. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `added_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--added_by))
- `created_at` (String) When they were added.
- `member` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--member))

<a id="nestedatt--items--added_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.added_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
